extracted.intended_audience: general readers and practitioners in public relations/online reputation management
extracted.subtask_description: A broad encyclopedic overview of reputation management, covering definitions, online and offline strategies, common tactics, ethical issues, historical examples, and vulnerabilities of reputation systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of reputation management
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation management is the deliberate influence, control, enhancement, or concealment of an individual's or group's reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a marketing technique used to modify a person's or a company's reputation in a positive way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online reputation management (ORM) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Online reputation management involves overseeing and influencing the search engine results related to products and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes monitoring social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, etc.), addressing potentially damaging content, using customer feedback to solve problems, and search engine reputation management designed to counter negative search results and elevate positive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline reputation management scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Offline reputation management shapes public perception of an entity outside the digital sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popular controls include social responsibility, media visibility, press releases in print media, and sponsorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent long-term reputation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a long-term reputation strategy that is consistent across all web-based channels and platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORM includes traditional PR strategies but emphasizes cross-channel consistency and sustained efforts rather than one-off fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress negative search results and elevate positives
rubrics_metrics.description: A major part of reputation management involves suppressing negative search results, while highlighting positive ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactics to accomplish this include creating positive content, SEO, and authoritative placements to push down harmful items in search rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aligning self-perception with public perception
rubrics_metrics.description: For businesses, reputation management usually involves an attempt to bridge the gap between how a company perceives itself and how others view it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of customer feedback and proactive engagement to address issues before they damage reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of search-engine result modification tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Modifying the way results from searches are displayed (for example via white papers or prioritising positive customer testimonials) to push down negative content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly aimed at changing search-result prominence rather than removing content at source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing original positive websites and social profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing original, positive websites and social media profiles with the aim of outperforming negative results in a search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create owned content that can rank for branded queries and present favorable information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting online press releases to authoritative websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting online press releases to authoritative websites in order to promote brand presence and suppress negative content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an ORM tactic to create positive, indexable signals on reputable domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal takedown and takedown-pretending requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting legal take-down requests if they have or pretend to have been libeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be legitimate where libel occurs, but the page notes some actors may 'pretend' to be libeled as a tactic to remove content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Securing mentions on high-ranking third-party sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting mentions of the business or individual on third-party sites that rank highly on Google.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party, authoritative placements can help crowd out negative content in search results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of fake positive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Creating fake, positive reviews of the individual or business to counteract negative ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a common tactic; this practice is unethical and has led to lawsuits and platform enforcement actions (e.g., Amazon suing fake reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of spambots and denial-of-service attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Using spambots and denial-of-service attacks to force sites with damaging content off the web entirely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a tactic (citation needed); represents illegal and unethical behavior with significant risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astroturfing / sockpuppeting on third-party sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Astroturfing third-party websites by creating anonymous accounts that create positive reviews or lash out against negative ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also referenced as 'wikiturfing' or 'wikiwashing' when applied to Wikipedia; obfuscates corporate role and misleads audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactively offering free products to prominent reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively offering free products to prominent reviewers to secure favorable coverage or reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common PR tactic but raises disclosure and impartiality issues depending on disclosure and platform rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing online mug shots and embarrassing images
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing online mug shots and removing or suppressing images that are embarrassing or violate copyright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some services charge fees to remove such images; this raises ethical concerns and may be temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive response to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively responding to public criticism stemming from recent changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of crisis and reputation management: engage rapidly and constructively to mitigate reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbidding comments as a control tactic
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbidding any comments on a platform or content as a means of controlling public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppresses user feedback and can reduce visible negative commentary but may also harm credibility and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wikiturfing / wikiwashing (Wikipedia manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contacting Wikipedia editors to remove allegedly incorrect information and obfuscating the role of profit-seeking corporations while promoting a misleading image consistent with wiki values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly criticized as misleading; manipulating encyclopedia entries can provoke exposure and reputational backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical disclosure and avoidance of deceptive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to draw the line for disclosure, astroturfing, and censorship is widely disagreed upon; hiring staff to pose as bloggers without disclosing they were paid is an unethical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exposure of unethical reputation management may itself harm the firm's reputation; firms should consider disclosure norms and legal/ethical boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective client acceptance on ethical grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Many firms are selective about clients they accept and may avoid individuals who committed violent crimes who are looking to push information about their crimes lower on search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ethical screening practice used by reputation firms to limit harmful or illegitimate engagements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability of reputation metrics to gaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation-scoring systems (e.g., Naymz's RepScore) can be easily deceived by small groups who reciprocally provide positive feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies show high reputation levels can be achieved by coordinated reciprocal endorsements, illustrating limits of such metrics' reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on removals and realism about outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation managers generally cannot remove major government-related news stories from established publications or court records; removal efforts may be limited and expensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be realistic about what can be suppressed and note that some removals are temporary; litigation and public records often remain accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost and accessibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation management can be an expensive service that many people cannot afford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High cost limits access to such services; some who might benefit (e.g., victims of public shaming) may be unable to pay for remediation.
